instruction: I'm thinking of adding some living space to my home. What are my options?
reply: The Rent a Room scheme makes the first £7,500 a year of rent tax free if you let a furnished room in the home you live in, and there is nothing to declare below that. Take a month's rent as a deposit and give a written licence agreement rather than a tenancy, so it stays easy to end.

instruction: I have a lot of homework to do and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Can you help me organize it?
reply: Count the days you actually have (sleep and school nights are not revision), list the topics per subject, and give each topic one block rather than one subject one day: three blocks a day is a real day's work. Put the subject you dread first, in the morning.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to engage my students in the classroom. Have you heard of game-based learning?
reply: Give every child a ball and keep them moving: ten minutes of a game with a ball each (dribble and freeze), fifteen of one skill in a small game (passing through gates, or 1v1 to a line), then twenty minutes of small-sided matches, four a side, no keepers. No queues, no laps, no long instructions — if they stand still for more than a minute you lose them.

instruction: I'm interested in track and field events. What's the most popular one?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources to learn about history. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Essay subjects are learned by writing answers, not by reading the notes again: get the mark scheme for your board, write three timed past questions a week and plan the other two in a spider diagram. Mark your own answer against the criteria and count what you missed - a point you did not make, a quote, the evaluation sentence at the end - because the marks are in the structure as much as the knowledge.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I've been thinking about walking more.
reply: About 7,000 to 8,000 steps a day is where most of the benefit is - the health gain levels off there rather than at 10,000, which came from a 1960s pedometer advert - so add a daily twenty minutes on top of what you already do rather than chasing a round number. If you are a long way off, two ten-minute walks beat one long one because they are easier to keep up, and the walking you do getting about counts.

instruction: I'm looking for information about famous artists. Can you tell me about Vincent van Gogh?
reply: Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519) was an Italian painter, engineer and anatomist: the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper on one side, notebooks of flying machines and dissected bodies on the other. Fewer than twenty of his paintings survive, and it is the range of his curiosity that made him famous.

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in our oceans. Is it really a big problem?
reply: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning coal and oil mix with water in the air and fall as weak acid. It harms trees and lakes; filters on power stations and cleaner fuel have cut it a lot since the 1980s.

instruction: I'm learning to code and I was wondering what programming languages are used for web development.
reply: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language: it is the set of tags that say what each part of a web page is - a heading, a paragraph, a link - and the browser turns those tags into the page you see. It is not a programming language and it cannot do arithmetic, which is what CSS and JavaScript are for.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for an online learning platform to use with my students. Have you heard of Google Classroom?
reply: Write in your own words, in short lines, and do not try to transcribe: you are making a map to come back to, not a transcript. Leave a wide margin for questions after the lesson and add them the same evening, in five minutes, while it is still fresh.

instruction: I'm learning about endangered species. What is biodiversity?
reply: A species is a group of living things that can breed together and produce fertile young: dogs are one species, and a horse and a donkey are different species because their mule offspring cannot have young. Members of a species share most of their genes.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm trying to improve my technique. What's the most important thing to focus on?
reply: Nothing new on the day: the shoes, socks and kit you did your long runs in, plus your race number, safety pins, a bottle, and the gels or sweets you have practised with. Eat the breakfast you have tested, get there an hour early, and set off slower than feels right.

instruction: I'm learning about renewable and non-renewable resources in school. What's the difference between the two?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, so I was thinking of starting a walk-to-work initiative in my neighborhood. Do you think it's a good idea?
reply: Walking alone will not do it - what you eat decides most of it - but 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day is a fair target, and the gain is that it burns a little and keeps you from sitting down all day. The quicker half is the plate: a smaller portion of the starch, more protein and vegetables, and no drinks with sugar in.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites for interactive simulations?
reply: *Wow in the World* is the best one to start with: science stories with two silly hosts, made for 5 to 8 year olds. *Story Pirates* turns stories children send in into sketches and songs, and *Circle Round* tells a folk tale in fifteen minutes with a proper cast.

instruction: I'm thinking of upgrading my computer's operating system. What's the difference between Windows and macOS?
reply: An SSD has no moving parts, so the machine starts in seconds and apps open at once; a hard drive is a spinning disc and only wins on price for each gigabyte. For a laptop the SSD is the one upgrade that makes an old machine feel new - a 500GB one is cheap now and cloning the old disk across is a job a shop will do in an hour.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a new puppy and I'm wondering how I can help it get along with my other pets.
reply: The day is the whole job: a short walk first thing, a proper one later, a last five minutes before bed, a garden break after every meal, and food twice a day for an adult or three or four small meals for a puppy. Then the boring parts that keep him well - a microchip (law in the UK), a yearly check and booster at the vet, worming every three months and flea treatment monthly, and insurance taken out before anything is wrong with him.

instruction: What causes the seasons to change?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my social studies homework. What is geography?
reply: Longitude is how far east or west of Greenwich a place is, measured in degrees up to 180 each way, and it is what sets your time zone. Sailors could find their latitude for centuries before they could find their longitude, which is why accurate clocks were so valuable.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'm looking for some relaxation techniques. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Do one small thing you used to enjoy today, at half enthusiasm, because mood follows action more often than it arrives on its own: a walk to the shop, a phone call, ten minutes of a game you liked. Then stack the three things that lift a low mood most reliably - daylight within an hour of waking, 20 minutes of walking, and one person you really talk to rather than message - and keep bedtime and meals at the same time, because a sad week wrecks both and then feeds itself.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school. What's the difference between a carnivore, an herbivore, and an omnivore?
reply: A herbivore is an animal that eats only plants: a cow, a rabbit, a deer, a caterpillar. Its teeth grind and its gut is long enough to break down plant fibre, which is why it spends much of the day eating.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: You can eat well without cooking if you build the plate from the shop: a bag of salad or a punnet of tomatoes, ready-cooked chicken or a tin of tuna or chickpeas, and bread, couscous or a microwave pouch of rice. Frozen veg straight from the microwave is the cheapest half-plate of vegetables there is, and a pot of yogurt with fruit is pudding.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated. What are some water-rich foods I can eat?
reply: Aim for a palm-sized portion of protein at each meal - eggs, milk or yoghurt at breakfast, beans, lentils or chicken at lunch, fish or mince at dinner - which lands most adults near the 0.75g per kilo of body weight they need. Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned fish, eggs, tofu and lentils are the cheapest ways to add it.

instruction: It's raining outside, what should I wear?
reply: That is a question about the hours you will actually be out, not about the day: under about 10 degrees, yes, and a proper coat with a jumper under it if you will be standing about; between 10 and 18 a jumper and something windproof is enough, and over 18 you carry the coat rather than wear it. Rain decides it more often than cold does, so a waterproof beats a warmer one that lets water through, and the bits that feel it first are the neck, ears, hands and feet.

instruction: I'm starting a vegetable garden. What are some easy vegetables to grow?
reply: Fry them into a hash: chop them small, start with an onion and a pinch of salt, and let them crisp at the edges before you add anything wet. Roasted vegetables are better through pasta with garlic and a spoonful of the cooking water, and anything soft goes into soup with stock and a blender.

instruction: I'm planning a vacation to Europe and I'm looking for suggestions on historical landmarks to visit.
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my family about important decisions. Do you have any tips?
reply: Tell them early, in a call rather than a text, and give them the plan instead of only the no: 'We're staying here this year and we'll come up in January.' Say it once, then let them be disappointed without arguing them out of it - 'I know, and this is what we've decided.' Offer one concrete thing (a video call on the day, a visit you both get to look forward to) so the conversation ends on something instead of a silence.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. Do plants respond to their environment?
reply: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis: they take carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil and use sunlight to turn them into sugar. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light, and oxygen is released as a by-product.

instruction: I'm looking for a new way to cook my favorite beef stew. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Mash a drained tin of black beans or chickpeas with a grated small onion, a handful of breadcrumbs, a spoon of tomato puree and an egg to bind it - or a flax egg, a tablespoon of ground flaxseed in three of water, left ten minutes - then chill the mix twenty minutes so the patties hold. Shape them 2cm thick and fry 4 to 5 minutes a side, or bake them 20 minutes at 200C (180C fan).

instruction: I'm feeling unwell and I'm not sure if I should go to the doctor.
reply: Feeling under the weather means a bit unwell - off colour, not seriously ill. What is wrong - sore throat, tired, sick?

instruction: I'm learning to play the guitar. What's the difference between a chord and a scale?
reply: A mandoline is a flat board with a blade set at an adjustable height, for slices of even thickness - 2mm potato for dauphinoise, cabbage for slaw - which a knife cannot match for speed. It is also the sharpest thing in most kitchens: use the hand guard, or a cut glove, every time, and stop while there is still a knuckle's width of vegetable left.

instruction: I'm a huge music fan. I've been to a few concerts and I was wondering what it's like backstage.
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I love going to the mall to look at the seasonal displays. What's your favorite season for window shopping?
reply: In a British city park in winter you'll usually see robins, blackbirds, blue tits, great tits, pigeons, crows and magpies, with gulls and starlings on the grass. Look in the bushes and bare trees rather than the open lawn, and early morning is the busiest time.

instruction: I'm looking for free online educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites?
reply: Believe them first and write down what happened, with dates and names, then ask the school for a meeting with the head of year rather than the class teacher alone. Ask what the school will do and when, and keep checking in with your child; if nothing changes in a few weeks, put it in writing and ask to see the head.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What's the main cause?
reply: Gases in the air, mainly carbon dioxide and water vapour, let sunlight in but absorb the heat that bounces back off the ground, much like glass in a greenhouse. That keeps the Earth about 33C warmer than it would be.

instruction: I'm planning a retirement party for my mom. What are some common family celebrations?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm learning about volcanoes in school and I was wondering, what is a volcano?
reply: Deep underground, rock melts into magma, which is lighter than the rock around it and rises. It collects in a chamber until the pressure forces it up through a vent, and it erupts as lava, ash and gas.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the nervous system does.
reply: Nerves and gut share the same wiring: adrenaline diverts blood to your muscles and slows digestion, so your stomach feels fluttery or churny. Slow breathing helps because it switches the body back toward rest, and it passes once the moment does.

instruction: I'm planning a last-minute trip to Paris. What's the weather like this time of year?
reply: Pack for 2 to 8C, wind and rain: a waterproof coat with a hood, warm layers you can take off indoors, and shoes you can walk a hill in. It gets dark around 4pm in December, so a small torch and plans for the afternoon indoors help.

instruction: I have two kids, a boy and a girl. What are some fun activities to do with them?
reply: Give every child a ball and keep them moving: ten minutes of a game with a ball each (dribble and freeze), fifteen of one skill in a small game (passing through gates, or 1v1 to a line), then twenty minutes of small-sided matches, four a side, no keepers. No queues, no laps, no long instructions — if they stand still for more than a minute you lose them.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school. What's the difference between a balanced and an unbalanced force?
reply: Magnetism is the force a magnet exerts on other magnets and on iron, nickel and cobalt, carried by a magnetic field around the magnet. Like poles repel and opposite poles attract, and a compass needle is a tiny magnet lining up with Earth's field.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What are climate models?
reply: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere instead of letting it escape to space. That extra heat raises average temperatures, melts ice and makes extreme weather more likely; the science is settled, though predicting any one storm is not.

instruction: I'm looking for some new recipes to try out, do you have any family recipes you can share?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking of taking a nap. What's the best time for a nap?
reply: Keep a nap to 20 minutes and take it before 3pm, or you'll feel groggy and sleep worse that night; 30 to 60 minutes is where the grogginess lives, so set an alarm. Skip it if you already lie awake at night, and if you need one every afternoon for weeks, that is worth a word with the GP, especially with low mood, thirst or weight loss.

instruction: How are the Chicago Cubs doing this season?
reply: One team bats to score runs and the other bowls and fields to get them out; an over is six balls, and an innings ends when ten batters are out or the overs run out. You are out if the ball hits your stumps, if a fielder catches it before it bounces, if you are run out, or leg before wicket — hit on the pads by a ball that was going to hit the stumps.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do dreams affect our mental health?
reply: Nightmares usually follow stress, late food, alcohol or a heavy film before bed, so start there. If the same one keeps coming back, write it down in the day and rehearse a different ending a few times: that is the technique that works.

instruction: What are the most popular gaming platforms right now?
reply: Match it to the age and the room rather than to the adverts. Under about ten, a Nintendo Switch is the safe first console: it comes with a game, works handheld or on the television, and Nintendo's free parent app sets a daily limit and turns it off at bedtime.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with my friends. What types of board games are there?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: I'm planning to do some online shopping and I'm worried about security. What can I do to protect myself?
reply: Match it to the age and the room rather than to the adverts. Under about ten, a Nintendo Switch is the safe first console: it comes with a game, works handheld or on the television, and Nintendo's free parent app sets a daily limit and turns it off at bedtime.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultures. Can you tell me about a traditional holiday in Japan?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a wheel and axle?
reply: A turbine is the jet's opposite: wind pushes the blades, the blades turn a shaft through a gearbox, and a generator turns that spin into electricity. The blades are long and thin because the force goes up with the square of their length, and the machine feathers them out of the wind when it is too strong to use.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Thai cuisine. What's a popular Thai dish?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm new to the company and I'm trying to figure out my commute options. Does the company offer a shuttle service?
reply: Pre-book it: the price at the barrier is often two or three times the pre-booked price for the same space, and the cheapest of all is usually a park-and-ride a few minutes out with a shuttle. Compare the total against the alternatives before you choose, because a week of parking often costs about what a taxi costs each way, and for two or three days the taxi, the train or a lift from a friend usually wins.

instruction: I'm having trouble telling time. Can you help me?
reply: Split your time in three: a few minutes going over yesterday's phrases out loud, most of it on new phrases said aloud and written down once, and a few minutes listening to something short at normal speed. Learn whole phrases you will use rather than grammar tables, and speak from the first week — even to yourself in the kitchen.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow. What should I bring?
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school and I'm having trouble understanding electrostatic force. Can you explain it to me?
reply: Rubbing two materials together can pull electrons from one to the other, leaving a charge that builds up on a surface. When you touch something, the charge jumps across as a small spark, which you feel as a shock.

instruction: I'm looking for information about government jobs. What are some main categories of government jobs?
reply: The cabinet is about 20 senior ministers picked by the prime minister, each running a department - the chancellor at the Treasury, the home secretary, the foreign secretary. It meets weekly to settle the big calls, and collective responsibility binds them: argue inside the room, then defend it outside or resign.

instruction: I'm looking for a new gaming platform. What's the difference between PlayStation and Xbox?
reply: PS stands for postscript, from the Latin post scriptum, meaning written after: the line you add once the letter is finished and signed. On a keyboard P.S.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get more vitamin D. What are some natural sources of it?
reply: Take 10 micrograms (400 IU) of vitamin D every day through autumn and winter, roughly October to March: the sun is too low in the sky here for your skin to make it, however grey or bright the day is. From April to September, short spells outside with hands and face uncovered is enough for most people, and oily fish, eggs and fortified cereal help the rest of the year.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I want to make a list. Can you help me with that?
reply: Build a sentence from the first letters (Never Eat Shredded Wheat for the compass), or tie items to places on a walk round your house - the sillier the image, the better it sticks. Mnemonics are good for lists and orders, useless for understanding; use them for the facts you keep dropping.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the violin. When was it invented?
reply: Isaac Newton (1643-1727) worked out the three laws of motion and the law of gravity, showing that the same force pulls a falling apple and holds the Moon in its orbit. He published it in the Principia in 1687, and he also worked out calculus at the same time as, and independently of, Leibniz.

instruction: I'm looking for a new blender. What are some popular brands?
reply: A stick blender is the wand you put straight into the pan or jug: soup, sauce, a smoothie, all blended where they are, with nothing to pour and one thing to wash. Keep the blade under the surface before you switch on or it spatters, and do not use it on boiling soup in a deep pan without taking the pan off the heat first.

instruction: I'm planning to renovate my bathroom and I'm looking for some ideas.
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas.

instruction: What is the Roman numeral for the number 5?
reply: Write the date in full and in one order: 10 March 2025 (British) or March 10, 2025 (American), with no th and no comma in the British form. In a letter, put it above the greeting; the ordinal - the tenth of March - is for speech.

instruction: I'm new to weightlifting and I want to start a gym routine. What's a good exercise for beginners?
reply: Buy one adjustable dumbbell or one kettlebell and nothing else to begin with: about 6 to 10 kg suits most beginners and 10 to 16 kg if you are already strong, and a used one goes for £40 to £80. Add a resistance band for about £10 and a step or a sturdy chair, and that covers squats, rows, presses and carries - a mat only if your floor is hard.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm not sure how often I should trim his nails.
reply: Take a sliver off at a time and stop at the pink centre, the quick: hold a torch under the nail and it shows as a darker oval to aim short of. Cut straight across rather than at an angle, keep the treats coming, and if he hates it do one nail a day.

instruction: I'm looking for some fashion tips for the upcoming fall season. What are some popular colors this year?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for something to watch this weekend. What sports are on TV?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm thinking of remodeling my kitchen. What are some popular materials for countertops?
reply: A trivet is the stand that keeps something hot off the table or the counter - a pan, a casserole, a slow cooker's pot. Wooden, cork, stone or metal, all it does is hold the heat away from the surface; a folded dry towel does the same job when the trivet is not there.

instruction: I'm looking for a new baseball bat. What types are available?
reply: Start with very little: trainers or astro boots, shorts or leggings, a water bottle and, for football or hockey, shin pads. Clubs lend sticks, bats and bibs to beginners, so email and ask what they provide before you buy anything.

instruction: I have a brother and a sister, and we all live together. What are some ways we can share household responsibilities?
reply: Pay in by what each of you earns, not by halves: if one of you takes home 60% of the joint income, that person covers 60% of the bills. Keep a joint account for rent, bills and food, keep your own accounts for the rest, and look at it together once a month rather than arguing over individual receipts.

instruction: I'm trying to find my personal style. Where do I start?
reply: Measure in a bra or a thin top, tape snug but not tight and level all the way round, and write three numbers in cm: bust at the fullest point, waist at the narrowest above the navel (bend sideways and the crease is it), and hips at the widest, about 20cm below the waist. Add your height and inside leg and you have everything a size guide asks for.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my wardrobe. What are the current street style trends?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: What is an echo?
reply: In the call settings pick the right microphone and speaker instead of the default, because a monitor or headset often takes them over. Raise the input volume to about 80%, sit closer to the mic, and use headphones on both ends to stop the echo; if it is an older relative, a tablet is easier than a phone.

instruction: I'm looking for a running community to join. Do you know any popular ones?
reply: Adult lessons at your local pool are the fastest route: most run classes for complete beginners, often in small groups, and every instructor has taught adults who are frightened of the water. Book a course rather than one lesson, start in the shallow end with floats, and ask for an instructor who is used to nervous beginners.

instruction: I'm looking for information about music awards. What's the biggest music award show?
reply: The Grand Slams are the four biggest tournaments: the Australian Open in January, the French Open at Roland-Garros on clay, Wimbledon on grass, and the US Open. Winning all four in the same year is a calendar Grand Slam - Rod Laver did it in 1969 and Steffi Graf in 1988.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, what kind of exercise does it need?
reply: For an older dog: a warm, soft bed away from draughts, a ramp or a low step for the sofa, shorter and more frequent walks, and a vet check twice a year. Keep its claws short, which is easy to forget when it walks less, and ask the vet about pain relief if it's slow to get up.

instruction: I'm thinking of adopting a pet, but I'm not sure what kind to get.
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I have a family with kids and we are thinking of getting a pet. What are some good types of pets for families with kids?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm interested in photography and I was wondering what's the best camera type for a beginner.
reply: Close every other app that might be holding the camera, then check the permission: on Windows, Settings > Privacy & security > Camera, and on a Mac, System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera, and switch your app on. A laptop with a sliding shutter over the lens is the other common one.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cooking technique to try. What's braising?
reply: Score the skin, pour a kettle of boiling water over it, dry it and rub in plenty of salt and a little oil, then roast it at 220C for 30 minutes and 180C after that, without basting or covering it, and if the skin is still soft once the meat has rested cut the crackling off and grill it for 5 minutes on a rack.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What colors do you think I should start with?
reply: Draw what is in front of you, not from memory: a mug, your own hand, the chair opposite. Ten minutes a day beats a long session at the weekend, one object a day for a fortnight, and use a soft pencil (2B) on cheap paper so you are not afraid of it.

instruction: I've always been curious about how mountains affect the culture of people living near them. Can you tell me a little bit about that?
reply: A rain shadow is the dry side of a mountain range: air is forced up the windward side, drops its rain there, and comes down the other side warm and dry. Deserts like the one east of the Rockies sit in a rain shadow.

instruction: I want to improve my cardiovascular health. What are some good exercises for that?
reply: Start with what you can repeat three times a week: a 20 to 30 minute walk, two short strength sessions and some balance work, and add a little each week. Strength training twice a week matters more after 50 than a hard cardio session, because it is what keeps muscle and bone.

instruction: I'm looking for some DIY home decor ideas. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Dress for standing about outdoors: shorts or jeans and a light top, with a jumper for when the sun goes in. Leave the white things and the dry-clean-only at home, because there's smoke, grass and someone with a ketchup bottle.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting techniques?
reply: Three that work with children, easiest first: flapjack (no oven hands, just stirring and a flat tin), fairy cakes (they can fill the cases and ice them once cool) and shortbread (three ingredients, and cutting shapes is the fun part). Give the little ones the measuring and the stirring and keep the oven and the hob to yourself, and expect it to take twice as long as it would alone.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What are some examples of simple machines in everyday life?
reply: A weight or a wound spring stores the energy, a gear train slows it down, and an escapement lets it out one tick at a time - that tick is what moves the hands at a steady rate. A pendulum or balance wheel sets the rhythm, which is why a grandfather clock keeps good time and a cheap watch drifts.

instruction: Our school is having a science fair next week. What kind of projects do you think would be good for it?
reply: Make the shape, not the whole outfit: black leggings and a black top read as almost anything, then one thing does the work - a cardboard box for a robot or a rocket, a bin bag and a belt for a cape, a paper plate and elastic for a mask, a stripy top and an eye patch for a pirate. Paint it the night before, not the morning of, and ask the party's theme first.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my office more comfortable. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Stand up and move for two minutes every half hour, drink water, and put a bright light on your face — sleepiness at a desk is often boredom plus warm air. Do the hardest thing first and leave the reading for when you are flagging.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do weighted blankets really help?
reply: The things that work: same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after early afternoon, not much alcohol in the evening (it wakes you in the second half of the night), a cool dark room, and getting out of bed if you're awake for more than 20 minutes. Screens off half an hour before bed and a short walk most days help more than any app.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, and I want to know if agility training is good exercise for them.
reply: Five minutes of walking for each month of age, twice a day, so three months is about fifteen minutes a time and six months about half an hour. Until the vaccinations are done, keep him off the ground where other dogs go and let him play in the garden instead; free running and stairs are the things to hold back on while his joints form.

instruction: What are negative numbers?
reply: Use a number line: adding a negative moves you left, subtracting a negative moves you right, so 5 - (-3) is 8. Multiplying or dividing two negatives gives a positive, and one negative gives a negative: -2 x -3 is 6, and -6 / 2 is -3.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What makes a bedroom comfortable for sleep?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms to improve my skills. Have you heard of Skillshare?
reply: Ask three or four people who have just passed and book a single lesson with the one they liked most - a good instructor is the thing that makes lessons worth the money, and one lesson tells you more than any advert. Look for someone approved by the DVSA (an ADI badge on the windscreen), a quiet manner, and a lesson plan rather than being driven round for two hours.

instruction: I'm having trouble talking to my family about my feelings. Do you have any advice?
reply: Break the silence with something small and concrete rather than a big talk: a photo with 'saw this and thought of you - how are you doing?' on it, or a practical question about a parent or a house you both care about. Don't relitigate the argument in the first message - the point is a door left open.

instruction: I'm learning about shapes in nature. What shapes do we see in flowers?
reply: Sunlight bends as it enters raindrops, reflects off the back and bends again on the way out, which splits it into colours. You only see one with the sun behind you and rain in front, and the red band is always on the outside of the arc.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the circulatory system does.
reply: Cholesterol is a waxy fat the body needs for cell walls and hormones, and the liver makes most of it; the rest comes from food. The number that matters most is the LDL ('bad') part, which can clog arteries, and diet, exercise and sometimes a statin bring it down.

instruction: I'm looking for information about upcoming concerts in my area. Do you know any good venues?
reply: The side streets five to ten minutes further out are where the free and cheap spaces are: read the sign at the entrance, because a residents' bay or a one-hour limit is what the tickets come from. For a station or a town centre, the station car park or a park and ride is usually cheaper than the multi-storey, and the parking apps (RingGo, PayByPhone, JustPark) show the live price and let you top up from your phone.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ways to make my lectures more engaging for my students. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Write the one sentence you want people to remember, then build three slides around it and cut the rest. Practise out loud twice, standing up, timing it, and take a one-page note instead of reading the slides; the first 30 seconds scripted and the rest in headings is what keeps a talk calm.

instruction: I'm concerned about the apps on my phone. What kind of permissions do they usually ask for?
reply: An app is a program built for a phone or tablet, installed from the store that came with the device - the App Store on an iPhone, the Play Store on Android. It runs on the phone itself and keeps its own data, so an app and the website of the same name can hold different things, and deleting the app usually takes its data with it.
